speakingFunction: 과거의 상태나 느낌을 짧게 평가할 때

examples.english: It was difficult.
It was easy.
It was strange.
It was interesting.
It was confusing.
It was unexpected.
It was frustrating.

speakingFunction: 과거 상황을 하나의 명사로 규정할 때

examples.english: It was a mistake.
It was a problem.
It was a good experience.
It was a difficult situation.
It was a misunderstanding.

speakingFunction: 과거 상황에서 어떤 행동을 하기 어려웠음을 설명할 때
description: 가장 많이 쓰이는 'It was + 형용사 + to' 패턴의 대표형. 이 chunk를 통째로 외워두면 다른 형용사로 바로 교체할 수 있다.

examples.english: It was difficult to understand.
It was difficult to explain.
It was difficult to find the cause.
It was difficult to reproduce the issue.
It was difficult to make a decision.
It was difficult to get everyone's approval.

expansions.pattern: It was difficult for me to explain.
It was difficult for me to explain the issue.
It was difficult for me to explain the issue because I didn't know the exact cause.
At first, it was difficult for me to explain the issue because I didn't know the exact cause, but eventually I figured it out.
expansions.description: 여러 chunk(because / eventually)를 연결해 하나의 긴 발화로 확장한 최종 단계

speakingFunction: difficult보다 조금 더 구어적으로 '힘들었음'을 말할 때

examples.english: It was hard to believe.
It was hard to tell what happened.
It was hard to keep up with the changes.
It was hard to focus during the meeting.
It was hard to say no.

speakingFunction: 어떤 일이 수월했음을 말할 때

examples.english: It was easy to fix.
It was easy to understand once he explained it.
It was easy to set up.
It was easy to follow the instructions.
It was easy to miss that detail.

speakingFunction: 과거에 어떤 행동이 중요했음을 강조할 때

examples.english: It was important to check twice.
It was important to tell the team early.
It was important to ask first.
It was important to keep it simple.
It was important to document the decision.

speakingFunction: 선택이 아니라 꼭 해야 했던 일을 설명할 때

examples.english: It was necessary to restart the server.
It was necessary to get approval first.
It was necessary to change the plan.
It was necessary to update the config.
It was necessary to slow down and double-check.
examples.korean: 속도를 늦추고 다시 확인할 필요가 있었어.

speakingFunction: 아무리 해도 할 수 없었던 일을 말할 때

examples.english: It was impossible to reproduce the bug.
It was impossible to meet the deadline.
It was impossible to predict the result.
It was impossible to reach him that day.
It was impossible to fit everything in one slide.
examples.korean: 슬라이드 하나에 다 담는 게 불가능했어.

speakingFunction: 누구에게 어려웠는지 사람을 명시하고 싶을 때
description: 'It was difficult to ...'에 'for + 사람'을 넣어 누구에게 어려웠는지 구체화한 확장형.

examples.english: It was difficult for me to understand.
It was difficult for us to find the cause.
It was difficult for them to reproduce the issue.
It was difficult for everyone to know what was happening.
It was difficult for me to explain it in English.

speakingFunction: 'difficult for'보다 구어적인 'hard for' 버전

examples.english: It was hard for us to find the cause.
It was hard for the team to agree on a plan.
It was hard for me to keep going.
It was hard for us to work remotely at first.
It was hard for her to say it out loud.
examples.korean: 그녀는 그걸 입 밖으로 꺼내기 힘들었어.

speakingFunction: 상황이 확실했다는 것을 말할 때

examples.english: It was clear that something was wrong.
It was clear that we needed more time.
It was clear that he didn't know the answer.
It was clear that the plan wasn't working.
It was clear that nobody had tested it.
examples.korean: 아무도 테스트를 안 했다는 게 분명했어.

speakingFunction: 'clear'보다 더 강하게 명백했음을 말할 때

examples.english: It was obvious that it wouldn't work.
examples.korean: 그게 안 될 거라는 게 명백했어.

examples.english: It was obvious that she was upset.
It was obvious that we made a mistake.
It was obvious that the design needed changes.
It was obvious that no one had read the email.
examples.korean: 아무도 메일을 안 읽었다는 게 명백했어.

speakingFunction: 예상과 다르고 의아했던 상황을 말할 때

examples.english: It was strange that nobody noticed it.
examples.korean: 아무도 눈치 못 챘다는 게 이상했어.

examples.english: It was strange that it just stopped working.
It was strange that he didn't call back.
examples.korean: 그가 다시 전화 안 했다는 게 이상했어.

examples.english: It was strange that the error disappeared on its own.
It was strange that everyone was so quiet.

speakingFunction: 예상 밖이라 놀랐던 상황을 말할 때

examples: it worked on the first try

examples.english: It was surprising that it worked on the first try.
It was surprising that she agreed so quickly.
examples.korean: 그녀가 그렇게 빨리 동의했다는 게 놀라웠어.

examples.english: It was surprising that nobody complained.
It was surprising that the fix was so simple.
It was surprising how fast it got resolved.

speakingFunction: 결과적으로 다행이었던 일을 말할 때

examples.english: It was good that we checked it first.
It was good that we had a backup.
It was good that someone caught the bug early.
It was good that I asked before deploying.
It was good that we didn't rush it.

speakingFunction: 결과의 원인을 설명할 때

examples.english: It was because I was tired.
It was because the server was down.
It was because we didn't have enough time.
It was because I misunderstood the question.
It was because there was a problem with the system.

speakingFunction: 무엇을 위한 것이었는지 목적/용도를 말할 때
description: 'It was to V'(~하려는 목적/행동)와 의미가 다르다. 'It was for + 명사/-ing'는 용도를 말하고, 'It was to V'는 의도한 행동 자체를 말한다. 예: 'It was to test the system.'(시스템을 테스트하려는 거였어) vs 'It was for testing.'(테스트 용도였어)

examples.english: It was for testing.
It was for a customer.
It was for security reasons.
It was for testing the new feature.
It was for the demo tomorrow.
It was to test the system.

speakingFunction: 무엇에 관한 것이었는지 주제를 말할 때

examples.english: It was about the project.
It was about improving the process.
It was about solving the problem.
It was about finding a better way.
examples.korean: 더 나은 방법을 찾는 것에 관한 거였어.

examples.english: It was about the new API.

speakingFunction: 과거에 상태가 점점 변해가고 있었음을 말할 때 (단순 동명사가 아니라 변화/진행을 나타냄)

examples.english: It was getting better.
It was getting worse.
It was getting late.
It was getting complicated.
It was getting hard to keep track of everything.
examples.korean: 모든 걸 따라가기 점점 힘들어지고 있었어.

speakingFunction: 'getting'보다 약간 격식 있는 변화 표현

examples.english: It was becoming difficult to manage.
It was becoming obvious that we needed help.
examples.korean: 도움이 필요하다는 게 점점 분명해지고 있었어.

examples.english: It was becoming clear that the plan had to change.
examples.korean: 계획을 바꿔야 한다는 게 점점 분명해지고 있었어.

examples.english: It was becoming a real problem.
It was becoming too complicated to explain.

speakingFunction: 예상보다 시간이 오래 걸리고 있었던 상황을 말할 때

examples.english: It was taking too long.
It was taking forever to load.
It was taking longer than expected.
It was taking a toll on the whole team.
It was taking up most of my day.

speakingFunction: 자신의 의견을 말할 때 가장 기본이 되는 표현

examples.english: I think it's a good idea.
I think we should wait.
I think this will work.
I think there's a better way.
examples.korean: 더 나은 방법이 있을 것 같아.

examples.english: I think we're overcomplicating this.
examples.korean: 우리가 너무 복잡하게 만드는 것 같아.

speakingFunction: 대상에 대한 평가를 짧게 말할 때

examples.english: I think it's fine.
I think it's too risky.
I think it's a great idea.
I think it's worth trying.
I think it's the best option we have.
examples.korean: 우리가 가진 것 중 최선인 것 같아.

speakingFunction: 제안이나 권고를 할 때

examples.english: I think we should wait a bit.
examples.korean: 조금 기다리는 게 좋을 것 같아.

examples.english: I think we should talk to the team first.
examples.korean: 먼저 팀과 얘기하는 게 좋을 것 같아.

examples.english: I think we should try a different approach.
examples.korean: 다른 방법을 시도하는 게 좋을 것 같아.

examples.english: I think we should double-check before deploying.
examples.korean: 배포 전에 다시 확인하는 게 좋을 것 같아.

examples.english: I think we should keep it simple.
examples.korean: 단순하게 유지하는 게 좋을 것 같아.

speakingFunction: 문제의 원인에 대한 자신의 생각을 말할 때

examples.english: I think the problem is we didn't test enough.
examples.korean: 문제는 테스트를 충분히 안 한 것 같아.

examples.english: I think the problem is the config.
I think the problem is we're missing some information.
I think the problem is timing.
I think the problem is on our end.
examples.korean: 문제는 우리 쪽에 있는 것 같아.

speakingFunction: 현재 발생 중인 문제의 핵심을 설명할 때

examples.english: The problem is that it only happens sometimes.
The problem is that we don't have enough data.
The problem is that nobody owns this.
examples.korean: 문제는 이걸 담당하는 사람이 없다는 거야.

examples.english: The problem is that it's hard to reproduce.
The problem is that we're running out of time.

speakingFunction: 과거에 있었던 문제의 핵심을 설명할 때

examples.english: The problem was that the logs didn't show anything.
examples.korean: 문제는 로그에 아무것도 안 보였다는 거였어.

examples.english: The problem was that we assumed the wrong thing.
The problem was that the test data was outdated.
The problem was that two teams were editing the same file.
examples.korean: 문제는 두 팀이 같은 파일을 수정하고 있었다는 거였어.

examples.english: The problem was that I didn't check the docs first.
examples.korean: 문제는 내가 문서를 먼저 안 봤다는 거였어.

speakingFunction: 무언가를 하는 데 어려움을 겪었음을 말할 때

examples.english: I had trouble understanding the requirements.
I had trouble finding the right file.
I had trouble trying to log in.
I had trouble explaining it clearly.
I had trouble getting it to work on my machine.
examples.korean: 내 컴퓨터에서 작동하게 하는 데 애먹었어.

speakingFunction: 과거에 특정 대상에 문제가 있었음을 말할 때

examples.english: There was a problem with the server.
There was a problem with the connection.
There was a problem with the payment.
There was a problem with the design from the start.
There was a problem with how we handled it.

speakingFunction: 'problem'보다 좀 더 기술적/업무적인 뉘앙스로 이슈가 있었음을 말할 때

examples.english: There was an issue with the deployment.
There was an issue with the API response.
There was an issue with the login flow.
There was an issue with the data format.
There was an issue with the last release.

speakingFunction: 어떤 행동을 할 방법이 전혀 없었음을 말할 때

examples.english: There was no way to know in advance.
There was no way to avoid it.
There was no way to fix it in time.
There was no way to contact them.
There was no way to test it locally.

speakingFunction: 과거 특정 시기의 경험을 회상하며 말할 때

examples.english: There was a time when I almost gave up.
There was a time when everything went wrong.
There was a time when we had no backup at all.
There was a time when this happened every week.
There was a time when nobody believed it would work.
examples.korean: 아무도 이게 될 거라 믿지 않았던 때가 있었어.

speakingIntent: 과거 내 상태를 설명하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 과거 어떤 행동을 시도하고 있던 중이었음을 말할 때

examples.english: I was trying to fix the bug.
I was trying to explain the situation.
I was trying to finish it before the deadline.
I was trying to reach you all morning.
I was trying to keep things simple.

speakingIntent: 과거 내 상태를 설명하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 어떤 행동을 하기 직전이었음을 말할 때

examples.english: I was about to leave.
I was about to call you.
I was about to give up.
I was about to send the email when it crashed.
I was about to ask the same thing.
examples.korean: 나도 막 같은 걸 물어보려던 참이었어.

speakingIntent: 과거 내 상태를 설명하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 과거에 무언가를 걱정했음을 말할 때

examples.english: I was worried about the deadline.
I was worried about losing the data.
I was worried about making a bad impression.
I was worried about how they'd react.
I was worried about nothing, it turned out fine.

speakingIntent: 과거 내 상태를 설명하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 과거에 무언가를 고민/생각하고 있었음을 말할 때

examples.english: I was thinking about quitting.
I was thinking about the new approach.
I was thinking about what you said earlier.
examples.korean: 네가 아까 한 말을 생각하고 있었어.

examples.english: I was thinking about switching teams.
I was thinking about how to explain it better.
examples.korean: 어떻게 더 잘 설명할지 생각하고 있었어.

speakingIntent: 지금 하는 일을 설명하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 지금 어떤 행동을 시도하고 있음을 말할 때

examples.english: I'm trying to figure it out.
I'm trying to reproduce the bug.
I'm trying to get this working by tomorrow.
I'm trying to keep it simple.
I'm trying to understand what changed.

speakingIntent: 지금 하는 일을 설명하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 지금 진행 중인 작업/일을 말할 때

examples.english: I'm working on the new feature.
I'm working on a fix for this.
I'm working on the report right now.
I'm working on it, give me a minute.
I'm working on something similar.

speakingIntent: 지금 하는 일을 설명하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 무언가를 찾고 있는 중임을 말할 때

examples.english: I'm looking for a better solution.
I'm looking for the right file.
I'm looking for someone who knows this area.
examples.korean: 이 분야를 아는 사람을 찾고 있어.

examples.english: I'm looking for feedback on this.
I'm looking for a way to speed this up.
examples.korean: 이걸 빠르게 할 방법을 찾고 있어.

speakingIntent: 지금 하는 일을 설명하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 가까운 미래의 계획을 말할 때

examples.english: I'm going to fix this today.
I'm going to talk to the team about it.
I'm going to take a short break.
I'm going to try a different approach.
I'm going to double-check everything first.

speakingIntent: 지금 하는 일을 설명하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 좀 더 구체적인 계획을 말할 때

examples.english: I'm planning to release it next week.
I'm planning to refactor this module.
I'm planning to move to a new stack.
I'm planning to finish this by Friday.
I'm planning to take some time off next month.

speakingIntent: 해야 할 일을 말하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 지금 해야 하는 일을 말할 때

examples.english: I need to check this first.
I need to talk to my manager about it.
I need to fix this before lunch.
I need to think about it a bit more.
I need to get this done today.

speakingIntent: 해야 할 일을 말하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 선택의 여지 없이 해야 하는 일을 말할 때

examples.english: I have to leave early today.
I have to redo this from scratch.
I have to follow the process here.
I have to be honest with you.
I have to admit, I didn't expect that.

speakingIntent: 해야 할 일을 말하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 과거에 어쩔 수 없이 해야 했던 일을 말할 때

examples.english: I had to rewrite the whole thing.
I had to cancel the meeting.
I had to ask for help.
I had to stay late to finish it.
I had to make a quick decision.

speakingIntent: 해야 할 일을 말하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 그럴 필요가 없다고 말할 때

examples.english: I don't need to worry about that anymore.
I don't need to explain everything.
I don't need to be there in person.
I don't need to redo it, it's fine as is.
examples.korean: 다시 할 필요 없어, 이대로 괜찮아.

examples.english: I don't need to check twice, I already did.
examples.korean: 두 번 확인할 필요 없어, 이미 했어.

speakingFunction: 원하는 것을 직접적으로 말할 때

examples.english: I want to understand this better.
I want to try a different way.
I want to hear your opinion first.
I want to make sure this is right.
I want to keep things moving.

speakingFunction: 'want to'보다 정중하게 원하는 바를 말할 때

examples.english: I'd like to ask a question.
I'd like to get some feedback on this.
I'd like to schedule a call this week.
examples.korean: 이번 주에 통화 일정을 잡고 싶습니다.

examples.english: I'd like to clarify something.
I'd like to hear more about your plan.
examples.korean: 당신의 계획에 대해 더 듣고 싶습니다.

speakingFunction: 과거에 원했던 것을 말할 때

examples.english: I wanted to let you know earlier.
I wanted to avoid this situation.
I wanted to finish it myself.
I wanted to double-check before telling you.
I wanted to make a good first impression.

speakingFunction: 이유를 명확하게 설명할 때

examples.english: The reason is that we ran out of time.
The reason is that the requirements changed.
The reason is that it wasn't tested enough.
The reason is simple: nobody checked it.
examples.korean: 이유는 간단해: 아무도 확인 안 했어.

examples.english: The reason is that we underestimated the scope.

speakingFunction: 앞서 말한 이유의 결과를 이어서 말할 때

examples.english: That's why I decided to change it.
That's why we're behind schedule.
That's why I asked for help.
That's why it took so long.
That's why I wanted to double-check first.
examples.korean: 그래서 먼저 다시 확인하고 싶었던 거야.

speakingFunction: 현재 상황의 이유를 말할 때 ('it was because'의 현재형)

examples.english: It's because I'm still learning this area.
examples.korean: 아직 이 분야를 배우는 중이라서 그래.

examples.english: It's because the system is under maintenance.
It's because we changed the process recently.
It's because nobody flagged it earlier.
It's because the data hasn't synced yet.

speakingFunction: 지금은 안 하지만 예전엔 자주 했던 일을 말할 때

examples.english: I used to work night shifts.
I used to do this manually.
I used to live near here.
I used to be afraid of public speaking.
I used to think this was impossible.

speakingFunction: 예전의 상태나 신분을 말할 때

examples.english: I used to be nervous about this.
I used to be a complete beginner.
I used to be on a different team.
I used to be skeptical about it.
I used to be much slower at this.

speakingFunction: 예전에는 하지 않았지만 지금은 하는 일을 대비해서 말할 때

examples.english: I didn't use to like this kind of work.
I didn't use to care about it much.
examples.korean: 예전엔 이거에 별로 신경 안 썼어.

examples.english: I didn't use to notice these things.
I didn't use to check this every time.
I didn't use to trust automated tests.

speakingIntent: 최근에 해온 일을 말하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 일정 기간 동안 계속해온 일을 말할 때

examples.english: I've been working on this feature for a week.
I've been working on the migration.
I've been working on a side project lately.
I've been working on my English speaking.
I've been working on it off and on.

speakingIntent: 최근에 해온 일을 말하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 한동안 계속 시도해온 일을 말할 때

examples.english: I've been trying to reach him all week.
examples.korean: 일주일 내내 그에게 연락하려고 하고 있어.

examples.english: I've been trying to fix this issue since Monday.
examples.korean: 월요일부터 계속 이 이슈를 고치려고 하고 있어.

examples.english: I've been trying to learn this framework.
examples.korean: 이 프레임워크를 계속 배우려고 하고 있어.

examples.english: I've been trying to explain this more clearly.
examples.korean: 이걸 더 명확하게 설명하려고 계속 하고 있어.

examples.english: I've been trying to get some feedback.

speakingIntent: 최근에 해온 일을 말하고 싶을 때
speakingFunction: 한동안 마음속으로 고민해온 것을 말할 때

examples.english: I've been thinking about changing the approach.
examples.korean: 방법을 바꾸는 걸 계속 생각하고 있어.

examples.english: I've been thinking about what you said.
examples.korean: 네가 한 말을 계속 생각하고 있어.

examples.english: I've been thinking about moving to a new role.
examples.korean: 새로운 역할로 옮기는 걸 계속 생각하고 있어.

examples.english: I've been thinking about this a lot lately.
I've been thinking about how to improve this.
examples.korean: 이걸 어떻게 개선할지 계속 생각하고 있어.

speakingFunction: 확실친 않지만 그런 것 같다고 추측할 때

examples.english: It seems like it's working now.
It seems like everyone agrees.
It seems like this is the main issue.
It seems like something changed overnight.
It seems like we're on the same page.

speakingFunction: 시각적/상황적 단서로 추측할 때

examples.english: It looks like it's going to rain.
It looks like we're almost done.
It looks like the fix worked.
It looks like nobody's home.
It looks like this needs more testing.

speakingFunction: 좀 더 격식 있게 추측을 말할 때

examples.english: It seems that the plan needs adjusting.
It seems that there's a misunderstanding.
It seems that the data is incomplete.
It seems that most people prefer this option.
It seems that we missed something.

speakingFunction: 확신이 없을 때

examples.english: I'm not sure if this is the right approach.
I'm not sure if they got the message.
I'm not sure if it's worth the risk.
examples.korean: 그럴 가치가 있는 위험인지 잘 모르겠어.

examples.english: I'm not sure if this will scale.
I'm not sure if I explained that well.
examples.korean: 내가 그걸 잘 설명했는지 잘 모르겠어.

speakingFunction: 잘 모르겠다고 직접적으로 말할 때

examples: this is a bug or a feature

examples.english: I don't know if this is a bug or a feature.
I don't know if we have time for this.
I don't know if it's the same issue.
I don't know if that's a good idea.
I don't know if anyone else noticed.

speakingFunction: 무언가에 따라 결과가 달라진다고 말할 때

examples.english: It depends on how much time we have.
It depends on what the client wants.
It depends on the data size.
It depends on who you ask.
It depends on the situation.

speakingFunction: 확실친 않지만 알고 있는 선에서 말할 때

examples.english: As far as I know, it's already fixed.
As far as I know, nobody's working on that.
examples.korean: 내가 알기로는 아무도 그거 안 하고 있어.

examples.english: As far as I know, that's still the plan.
As far as I know, this hasn't happened before.
As far as I know, everyone approved it.

speakingFunction: 구체적인 예시를 들어 설명할 때

examples.english: For example, we could use caching here.
examples.korean: 예를 들면, 여기 캐싱을 쓸 수 있어.

examples.english: For example, this happened last week.
examples.korean: 예를 들면, 지난주에 이런 일이 있었어.

examples.english: For example, some users reported the same issue.
examples.korean: 예를 들면, 몇몇 유저가 같은 이슈를 신고했어.

examples.english: For example, take a look at this case.
For example, this is what I mean.
examples.korean: 예를 들면, 이게 내가 말하는 거야.

speakingFunction: 'for example'과 같은 의미로 조금 더 격식 있게 말할 때

examples.english: For instance, the login page is slow.
For instance, some fields are missing in the response.
examples.korean: 예컨대, 응답에 일부 필드가 빠져 있어.

examples.english: For instance, we lost a customer because of this.
For instance, this worked fine in staging.
For instance, take last quarter's numbers.

speakingFunction: 가정을 들어 설명을 시작할 때

examples.english: Let's say we have 1,000 users.
Let's say the deadline moves up by a week.
examples.korean: 예를 들어 마감이 일주일 당겨진다고 해보자.

examples.english: Let's say this fails in production.
examples.korean: 예를 들어 이게 운영에서 실패한다고 해보자.

examples.english: Let's say I'm wrong about this.
examples.korean: 예를 들어 내가 이거 틀렸다고 해보자.

examples.english: Let's say we go with option A.

speakingFunction: 생각할 시간을 벌면서 자연스럽게 설명을 시작할 때

examples.english: The thing is, I didn't know about it.
The thing is, we don't have enough time.
The thing is, it's more complicated than that.
The thing is, nobody told me.
examples.korean: 그게, 아무도 나한테 말 안 해줬어.

examples.english: The thing is, it worked yesterday.

speakingFunction: 앞서 한 말을 다시 풀어서 명확히 할 때

examples.english: What I mean is, we should slow down a bit.
examples.korean: 내 말은, 좀 천천히 해야 한다는 거야.

examples.english: What I mean is, this isn't urgent.
examples.korean: 내 말은, 이게 급한 건 아니라는 거야.

examples.english: What I mean is, I need more context.
examples.korean: 내 말은, 좀 더 맥락이 필요하다는 거야.

examples.english: What I mean is, it's not your fault.
examples.korean: 내 말은, 네 잘못이 아니라는 거야.

examples.english: What I mean is, let's double-check before we ship.
examples.korean: 내 말은, 배포 전에 다시 확인하자는 거야.

speakingFunction: 복잡한 내용을 짧게 요약해서 말할 때

examples: it broke because of a typo

examples.english: Basically, it broke because of a typo.
Basically, we're back on schedule.
Basically, nothing has changed.
Basically, we need more people on this.
Basically, it's the same problem as before.
